_about: Worked example of a rite-cadence wave plan (the artifact the human-validated planning conversation OUTPUTS). Modeled on a real run (an overworld-game rite, wave 3: warp/world-map ∥ residences) — the file lists, prompts, and gate commands are that repo's, kept as an illustration of the required specificity; replace them with YOUR rite's content. The runnable `waves` array below is a frontend wave; `_backend_wave_example` shows the NEW backend/migration capability as a reference snippet (add such waves to `waves`, backend-before-frontend, only when your repo configures the isolation scripts). Replace every __PLACEHOLDER__ token with real values, then pass the object as args to the `rite-cadence` workflow. `rite-cadence({ waves, worktree_path, branch, dry_run:true })` first to validate.
_rules: Replace __WORKTREE_PATH__ (absolute path to the ext/* worktree, e.g. <repo>/.haunt-wt/<rite-slug>), __RITE_ID__, and every __GHOST_ID_*__ (Ghost Hunting UUIDs) before running.

implementers[].files MUST be pairwise DISJOINT within a wave (that's what makes the shared worktree safe). A file two ghosts both need must be OWNED by exactly ONE implementer — route the other ghost's need through a prop/callback, or sequence them into separate waves.

Backend work rides waves flagged backend:true — they get a runner-owned scratch Postgres ({{db_url}} injected into gate_cmds; required there, rejected elsewhere), the engine-appended migration-gate (+ pg-smoke when the repo sets .isolation.pg_smoke) gates, and a HARD ownership check (realized files ⊆ declared). Backend waves sort BEFORE frontend waves. They require the repo to configure isolation.db_script + isolation.migration_gate (+ db_prefix); validatePlan refuses a backend wave otherwise.

A migration-producing wave is flagged migration:true and has EXACTLY ONE implementer. NEVER declare paths under a migrations versions/ directory (e.g. backend/migrations/versions/ or backend/alembic/versions/) — revision numbers depend on the live head; the runner detects the generated file at runtime, commits it under the primary ghost, and (when isolation.db_migrate is set) proves reversibility (downgrade to the pre-wave head → upgrade → drift gate) post-commit.

gate_cmds run from the worktree root and are repo-specific (use your repo's test commands from .ghost/config.json — .tests.frontend / .tests.backend). Frontend waves: frontend/byte-gate only. Backend waves: DATABASE_URL={{db_url}} TIMEOUT_SECS=1500 <tests.backend> (the pytest suite is often hermetic sqlite — the scratch DB is for migrate/seed/pg-smoke) plus targeted ruff.
primary_ghost_id must be one of the wave's ghost ids; harden/reconcile sweep, runtime-detected migration, and harden-fix commits are attributed to it.

stop_before / resume_from name a wave; use them for approval gates (e.g. stop_before a J1 wave). Resume payloads carry baseline_red — pass it back via args.baseline_red to skip re-deriving the baseline.
